headline: APOE2 may protect the brain from Alzheimer’s and aging
dek: A new lab study reveals how the longevity-linked APOE2 variant protects neurons from DNA damage and stress, offering a potential path for Alzheimer's therapies.
bullets: APOE2 neurons show less DNA damage and better repair than APOE3 or APOE4.
Adding APOE2 protein to APOE4 neurons reduced DNA damage signaling.
Older APOE2 mice had healthier aging markers in the hippocampus.
caveat: Findings are from cell and mouse studies; human benefits are not yet proven.

headline: Watching too much TV in midlife may shrink the brain
dek: A new study of 1,700 adults finds that frequent TV viewing in midlife is associated with smaller brain regions and more white matter damage in later years.
bullets: Frequent TV viewers showed smaller memory and decision-making brain areas.
White matter damage was more common in heavy TV watchers.
Sitting alone wasn't the culprit; mentally engaging jobs were healthier.
caveat: This observational study shows a link, not cause and effect.

headline: FDA warns of hidden drugs in sleep, skin, and bodybuilding products
dek: Regulators alert consumers to undeclared active ingredients in certain supplements.
bullets: FDA warns about hidden drugs in some sleep, skin, and bodybuilding products.
These products may contain undeclared active pharmaceutical ingredients.
Consumers should be aware of potential health risks from such products.
caveat: The FDA notice does not specify which products or ingredients are affected.
